title: How long a job posting stays open
question: For the jobs the City is advertising now, how many days lie between the posting date and the filing deadline, which postings are open five days or fewer, and which are for exempt posts or for classes with one or two holders?
finding: The City’s careers site listed 182 postings on 14 November 2026: 102 Permanent Civil Service, 37 Temporary Exempt, 33 Permanent Exempt, 10 Temporary Provisional Permanent Civil Service. 60 have no closing date and 94 give one that can be measured. The middle posting with a date is open 15 days (Permanent Civil Service: 17, Temporary Exempt: 14, Permanent Exempt: 14, Temporary Provisional Permanent Civil Service: 14). 12 are open five days or fewer, 6 of them exempt appointments and 3 permanent civil-service ones. 6 permanent civil-service or provisional postings show fewer than three days between the two dates, the minimum the Commission’s rule sets in business days. 3 of the dated postings are for a class with no more than two paid holders in fiscal 2026. This is the only direct test of “filled basically immediately” that the public record allows, and it covers current postings only: past announcements are not published.
how: A snapshot of the City careers site taken on 14 November 2026: every listed posting with its posting date, appointment type, job class and the filing deadline as printed. Days open is the printed deadline minus the posting date; where the wording is “on or after” a date, that date is the earliest the posting can close. Postings with no date in the deadline text are counted but not measured. Holders is the number of people paid in the class citywide in fiscal 2026. Shortest first. Civil Service Rule 110 requires examination announcements to be posted for a minimum period “not to be less than three (3) business days”.
limits: One day’s snapshot cannot show the past: nothing on disk says how long the posting ran for any job already filled, and the careers site keeps no archive. A short posting must meet the three-business-day minimum, and exempt posts are not examinations, so that rule may not reach them at all. A posting dated late on one day in universal time can be a day earlier in San Francisco, and the date is the one the page carries now, so a posting that was re-issued or extended shows its latest date and can look shorter than it was. A short window narrows who can apply; it does not show that a candidate was chosen beforehand. The recruitment file for each posting would show how many applied.
